matching_paragraphs: Prototype Rather than putting a large corpus in the prompt every time, train a small KV cache (the attention state a model builds from text) for it once. Self-study generates synthetic conversations about the corpus and trains the cache with a context-distillation loss. Plain next-token training was not competitive with in-context learning.12 The Stanford authors match in-context quality on long-context benchmarks with 38.6 times less memory.12 It pays off only with many queries against one stable corpus and an open-weight model you can train. Open code exists.

Prototype A reinforcement-learned trigger watches the model's reasoning and decides when a second module inserts latent tokens, which are internal vectors and not words. The authors report gains of up to 38.22% over two external-memory systems and up to 13.44% over a GRPO-trained baseline on eight benchmarks.13 Memory arrives as latent tokens instead of prompt text, at the price of training an added module. The official implementation publishes Weaver and Trigger training, evaluation scripts and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and SmolLM3-3B checkpoints for KodCode, GSM8K and TriviaQA, with no production support.14
